blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Coquitlam

items.t: Established-street house lots: freehold detached houses across the central streets under the City's small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996. Subdivision minimums as the City states them: 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size — the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.
City Centre edge sites

Bare-land strata: none verified: The form is contemplated by the zoning bylaw — Part 6, s.601(2) provides that bare land strata subdivision is permitted only if a roadway providing vehicular access to each strata lot is provided — but a permitted form is not stock.

Serviced vs unserviced, as the City states it: Critically for lot value: lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the City's SSMUH rules — so property-level septic or well status changes what a lot can do, and that status is UNVERIFIED parcel-by-parcel in the research.
ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for the sub-area is UNVERIFIED in the research; no ALR split is stated and none is invented. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any ALR rule.

Watercourse-shaped land: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses and s.523 covers riparian areas. A Fraser River floodplain designation for Central Coquitlam's residential streets: UNVERIFIED. Gross lot area is not buildable area on creek and ravine lots.

Hideaway Park (Coquitlam Hideaway Mobile Home Park) — 4200 Dewdney Trunk Road (Ranch Park). PAD-RENTAL PARK: The same marketing document notes the site falls within a "Shoulder Station Area" in the City's Transit-Oriented Development Strategy with potential to be rezoned to multifamily use — a redevelopment-risk fact a park buyer must weigh. Pad rent for any specific home: UNCONFIRMED (listing figures conflict).
Pine & Glen — 1175 Pinetree Way (Onni): It sells strata condominiums, not lots; the 186 rental apartments are rental-only.

No specific development application in Central Coquitlam beyond the above was verified: on a City development application page in the research: UNVERIFIED. Applications and rezoning proposals, where they exist, are documented as proposals only — never as for-sale inventory.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Coquitlam

items.t: Municipality: City of Coquitlam, BC — Central Coquitlam is the established central part of the city, around Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge. "Central Coquitlam" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report; an official City neighbourhood plan name for "Central Coquitlam" was not confirmed — the City plans this part of Coquitlam through its City Centre and Town Centre planning and the Transit-Oriented Areas framework. Boundaries: UNVERIFIED.

Nearby areas: Coquitlam West / Southwest Coquitlam to the west, City Centre (North Coquitlam in the board naming) to the north-east, Burke Mountain beyond, Maillardville to the south, Port Moody to the west.

Main roads: Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue, Pinetree Way and Guildford Way. Transit: the Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas serve the City Centre edge on Pinetree Way and Barnet Highway, and Coquitlam Central also has West Coast Express service; per-route bus numbers for the interior streets: UNVERIFIED. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based, in a three-tier district (elementary / middle / secondary). Settled locator chain for one sample address only: for 1169 Pinetree Way (Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch), the SD43 School Locator result is Glen Elementary, École Maple Creek Middle and Pinetree Secondary. SD43 schools named for central Coquitlam on district pages include Central Elementary School, Hillcrest Middle School and École Dr. Charles Best Secondary School (their street addresses were not confirmed); catchments for other addresses must be checked in the locator.

Parks and services: Town Centre Park and Como Lake Park are City park names in City records for this part of Coquitlam (addresses UNVERIFIED); City Centre Aquatic Complex and Evergreen Cultural Centre are in the City Centre area at the sub-area's east edge (addresses UNVERIFIED). Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, and Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, serve Coquitlam. Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the nearest hospital for this area. No shopping centre or grocery store for Central Coquitlam was verified on an official source in the research: UNVERIFIED.

Market context, labelled correctly (September 2026, SnapStats GVR September 2026 report): Central Coquitlam sub-area detached inventory 64 / solds 9 (14% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 36 / 5 (14% ratio); Coquitlam community detached median $1,455,000 ($550/sqft, 97% sale-to-list, 35 days on market) and attached median $625,000 ($687/sqft, 96%, 23 days). Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only). SnapStats has NO land category — none of these figures is a land figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Coquitlam

items.t: Bare-land strata block (no bare-land strata plan is documented in Central Coquitlam; stated for the form, which the zoning bylaw permits only with roadway access to each strata lot): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children). A listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (sub-area ALR status UNVERIFIED here; standing rules for completeness only): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; residence caps principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class three-tier ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — asserted here only as the standing three-tier rule; the research documents no farm-class parcel in Central Coquitlam, and a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR wherever it appears.

: City of Coquitlam property tax payment was due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance of current taxes after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants). Utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; the City's 2026 budget materials record an average-household total property-charges increase of $137 combined.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Coquitlam

items.t: The OCP changed in April 2026: Coquitlam adopted its Interim Official Community Plan (Bylaws 5511/5512) on April 27, 2026, superseding OCP No. 3479, 2001 — the City states it streamlined the old plan and added no new land-use policy except as provincial legislation required, with a fuller OCP update project anticipated to begin in 2027. A seller's disclosure or an old summary citing Bylaw 3479 is a generation out of date.

Services decide density here, not just lot size: the SSMUH unit counts (3 / 4 units) expressly exclude lots not connected to municipal water or sewer — two lots of identical size and zone on the central streets can carry different unit potential purely on servicing, and the research leaves parcel-level septic/well status UNVERIFIED.

The servicing bill has a name and a number: subdivision servicing in Coquitlam runs under Bylaw No. 3558, 2003 — a 2003 bylaw still being amended in July 2026 — including owner-paid City-installed signage and solicitor-approved statutory rights-of-way for services. A split priced without a Bylaw 3558 servicing estimate is priced blind.

The cheapest "land" in the sub-area is not land: Hideaway Park's pads rent — the park's own development-marketing document pairs its 68 pads / 5.76 acres with a Shoulder Station multifamily-rezoning note, so the tenure risk is documented in the seller-side material itself, not just in buyer caution.

faq.q: Which school district and schools serve Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: School District 43 (Coquitlam). For the sample address 1169 Pinetree Way, the SD43 locator result is Glen Elementary, École Maple Creek Middle and Pinetree Secondary; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the locator.

faq.q: What sold in Central Coquitlam in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached: 9 solds from 64 listings (14% sales ratio); condos & townhomes: 5 solds from 36 listings (14%). At the Coquitlam community level the detached median sale price was $1,455,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $625,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 64 houses listed with 9 sold in the month and 36 condos and townhomes listed with 5 sold in the month in Central Coquitlam. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Central Coquitlam a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 14%, a balanced market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 14%, a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Is there a vacant-lot subdivision I can buy into in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision or presale lot offering was verified. Land trades as built house lots on the Como Lake / Austin streets, strata units at the City Centre edge, and (at Hideaway Park) a home on a rented pad.

faq.q: Can a house lot add units?
faq.a: Yes under the City's SSMUH rules — up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes — but lots not connected to municipal water or sewer fall outside the rules, so confirm services and the exact zone first.

faq.q: Why can't I find the City Centre towers under "Central Coquitlam"?
faq.a: Because listing feeds label the verified tower cluster North Coquitlam / Canyon Springs / Town Centre, not Central Coquitlam — a "Central Coquitlam" board filter misses them.

faq.q: Is Hideaway Park a way to own cheap land in Coquitlam?
faq.a: You never own the land, and the document itself flags potential multifamily rezoning in a Shoulder Station Area — price the redevelopment risk, not a land value.

No — Pine & Glen (1175 Pinetree Way, Onni) is a presale of 705 strata condominiums plus 186 market-rental apartments in three towers over a podium, estimated completion 2028. Presale LOT offerings in the sub-area: zero verified.
